Q879275.label: Miguel Ydígoras Fuentes
Q879275.summary: José Miguel Ramón Ydígoras Fuentes was a Guatemalan military officer and politician who served as the 32nd president of Guatemala from 1958 to March 1963. He was also the main challenger to Jacobo Árbenz during the 1950 presidential election. Ydígoras previously served as the governor of the province of San Marcos.

Q83089579.label: 2020 Anguillan general election
Q83089579.summary: General elections were held in Anguilla on 29 June 2020. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, an Order in Council was made to allow the elections to be postponed until 11 September at the latest. However it was not invoked.

Q6544043.label: Liechtenstein trade initiative referendum, 1964
Q6544043.summary: A referendum on a trade initiative was held in Liechtenstein on 20 December 1964. The proposal was rejected by 62.5% of voters.

Q3722411.label: 1963 Hungarian parliamentary election
Q3722411.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Hungary on 24 August 1963. In the communist system the Hungarian Socialist Workers' Party was the only party that was allowed to contest the elections, and won 252 of the 340 seats, with the remaining 88 going to independents selected by the party.

Q14530731.label: 2013 Czech legislative election
Q14530731.summary: Early parliamentary elections were held in the Czech Republic on 25 and 26 October 2013, seven months before the constitutional expiry of the elected parliament's four-year legislative term.

Q2069163.label: 1947 Maltese general election
Q2069163.summary: General elections were held in Malta between 25 and 27 October 1947. They were the first elections held under universal suffrage for women and Agatha Barbara became the first woman elected to Parliament. These elections saw the Labour Party win 24 of the 40 seats.

Q4832427.label: Azerbaijani independence referendum, 1991
Q4832427.summary: An independence referendum was held in Azerbaijan on 29 December 1991, three days after the collapse of the Soviet Union. The result was 99.8% in favour of a constitutional act on the independence of the Republic of Azerbaijan, with turnout reported to be 95%.

Q315563.label: Katō Takaaki
Q315563.summary: Count Katō Takaaki, also known as Katō Kōmei, was a Japanese politician, diplomat, and Prime Minister of Japan from 1924 until his death on 28 January 1926, during the period which historians have called "Taishō Democracy".

Q741547.label: World Intellectual Property Organization Copyright Treaty
Q741547.summary: The World Intellectual Property Organization Copyright Treaty is an international treaty on copyright law adopted by the member states of the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) in 1996. It provides additional protections for copyright to respond to advances in information technology since the formation of previous copyright treaties before it.

Q130621611.label: Turkish Aerospace Industries headquarters attack
Q130621611.desc: 23 October 2024 terrorist attack on Turkish Aerospace Industries
Q130621611.summary: On 23 October 2024, seven people were killed and twenty-two people were injured in an armed attack on the headquarters of Turkish Aerospace Industries (TAI) in Kahramankazan, Ankara, Turkey. The two attackers were later killed. The Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) claimed responsibility for the attack.

Q1640107.label: Ifni War
Q1640107.desc: 1957–1958 armed conflicts in Spanish West Africa
Q1640107.img: My grandfather in the Ifni War Guerra de Ifni, 1958 (39782714325) (cropped).jpg
Q1640107.summary: The Ifni War, sometimes called the Forgotten War in Spain, was a series of armed incursions into Spanish West Africa by Moroccan insurgents that began in November 1957 and culminated with the abortive siege of Sidi Ifni.

Q41532587.label: Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan
Q41532587.summary: The Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan is a liberal political party in Japan. It is the primary centre-left party in Japan, and was the second largest party in the National Diet behind the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).

Q9387.label: Max Weber
Q9387.desc: German sociologist, philosopher, and political economist (1864–1920)
Q9387.summary: Maximilian Carl Emil Weber was a German sociologist, historian, jurist, and political economist who was one of the central figures in the development of sociology and the social sciences more generally. His ideas continue to influence social theory and research.
